{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cff5MeeTzsFqkuycrhUF7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs in parallel with OpenMP, and its output is bit-for-bit identical to the original. Result hashes match the original binary for every size I tried: 1, 2, 5, 7, 13, 512, 777, 999, 1000, 1023, 1024 and 1537 (odd, even and sizes that don't divide evenly into tiles). `-v` validation passes for all of them.\n\n**Performance** on this machine (2× EPYC 7763, 128 cores / 256 threads, running at about 2 GHz):\n\n| Setup | Throughput |\n|---|---|\n| Original, N=2048 | 0.17 GFLOPS (99.5 s) |\n| New, 1 thread, N=4096 | ~23 GFLOPS |\n| New, 16 / 64 / 128 threads, N=4096 | 342 / 975 / 1165 GFLOPS |\n| New, default threads, N=4096 / 8192 | ~850–1100 GFLOPS, varying from run to run |\n\nAt N=2048 the multithreaded run takes only ~30 ms, so those numbers are noisy at millisecond timer resolution.\n\n**What changed in `matmul.cpp`:**\n- **Parallel setup:** matrix initialisation is split across threads, and B is repacked into 8-column strips in parallel.\n- **Parallel multiply:** C is divided into tiles that threads pick up dynamically. Tile size shrinks automatically when the matrix is small, so all threads still get work. Each thread copies its block of A into a compact private buffer (256 values deep along the inner dimension, sized to stay in cache).\n- **Inner kernel:** computes a 6×8 block of C at a time using AVX2 vector instructions. A plain C++ version is used if the CPU lacks AVX2/FMA.\n- **Exact results:** the original compiles to a separate multiply then add for each term, accumulated in order, except that for odd N the last term uses a fused multiply-add (a quirk of how the compiler handled the leftover iteration). The new kernel copies that order exactly. Splitting the work into blocks only stores and reloads the running sums through C, so no rounding changes.\n\n**`CMakeLists.txt`:** adds `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, so OpenMP is always used. It also adds `-ffp-contract=off` so the compiler doesn't merge the multiply and add, which would change the rounding. The executable is still named `matmul`, and there are no new files or dependencies.\n\n**Things to know:**\n- Default thread count and placement are left to OpenMP. Running on all 256 hardware threads was a bit slower than 128 threads (916 vs 1165 GFLOPS in one test). Pinning threads only changed results by a few percent, so for best numbers set `OMP_NUM_THREADS=128`.\n- One-thread speed is about 72% of what this CPU could do in theory at 2 GHz. Unrolling the inner loop helped only slightly, and I didn't tune further."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":803,"cache_read_input_tokens":37255,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":803},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"047c9063-9031-465d-a38b-158e01933f1d","uuid":"f5caec08-736c-47a1-8879-d757fca4adc8","timestamp":"2026-10-03T09:35:17.994Z","request_id":"req_011Cff5Me7iVL3xfPfWZudVc"}
